title: Script-agnostic reflow of text in document images
venue: International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction with Mobile Devices and Services (MobileHCI)

summary.oneLiner: A script-agnostic technique reflows text in document images for small mobile screens, reaching over 95% segmentation accuracy across English, Hindi, Kannada and Arabic.
summary.overview: Reading scanned documents on a small phone screen is hard, and existing "reflow" tools, which rearrange text to fit the screen, mainly work for Latin-script text because they rely on script-specific features and optical character recognition (OCR). That leaves other scripts and mixed-script documents poorly served. This conference paper presents a reflow method that does not assume any particular script. On a corpus of 139 images in four very different languages it achieved over 95% segmentation accuracy, and a preliminary user study of a prototype suggested usability benefits.
summary.question: Can text in document images be reflowed for small mobile screens without relying on script-specific features or OCR, so that it works for non-Latin and mixed-script documents?
summary.method: A script-agnostic technique for segmenting and reflowing text in document images, evaluated on segmentation accuracy and in a preliminary user study of a prototype.
summary.data: A corpus of 139 document images in English, Hindi, Kannada and Arabic.
findings: Existing reflow solutions depend on script-specific characteristics and OCR, so they handle non-Latin and mixed-script documents poorly.
The proposed technique achieved over 95% segmentation accuracy on the 139-image corpus.
A preliminary user study of a prototype suggested usability benefits.
summary.whyItMatters: Because it does not depend on OCR, the approach could help mobile users read documents in scripts such as Hindi, Kannada and Arabic that Latin-focused tools handle poorly. It is an early computer-science paper, separate from Uppal's current marketing research.
